statement: A town surveyed $25$ households about how many pets they own. The results are shown in the table. $$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Number of pets} & \text{Number of households} \\ \hline 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array}$$ What is the median number of pets per household?

choices.misconception: I added up all the pets, 31, and divided by the 25 households, which gives the mean, not the median.
I took the middle of the list 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 in the first column, without counting how many households had each number.
I found the median of the household counts 7, 9, 6, 2 and 1, which is 6, instead of the median number of pets.

hints: The median is the middle value when all $25$ households are listed in order.
With $25$ values, the median is the $13$th value. Count down the table to see which row the $13$th household falls in.
The first $7$ households have $0$ pets and households $8$ through $16$ have $1$ pet. Where is household $13$?

solutions.reliable: There are $25$ households, so the median is the $13$th value in order. Households $1$ to $7$ have $0$ pets and households $8$ to $16$ have $1$ pet. The $13$th household has $1$ pet, so the median is $1$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
